//: What licence every model in the curated local-AI catalogue is under, and the terms behind each one.
`role` and `licence` are written BY HAND. `evidence` and `stamp` are machine-written by
`scripts/generate-local-catalog.mjs` straight from Hugging Face. The generator never DECIDES a
licence: every catalogued repo is a third-party GGUF conversion (bartowski / unsloth / ggml-org),
and a conversion's `license:` tag is a copy of the publisher's that can be stale, wrong, or
absent. `gated` is no proxy either — the conversions are all ungated even where google/gemma-3-*
When upstream's metadata moves, the stamp changes and the generator BLANKS the licence and
refuses to write the catalogue until a human looks again.
`models` is also the generator's SEED: the set of repos it fetches. One list, so a model cannot
be catalogued without a licence row, and the offline gate needs no access to the generator (which
imports an npm package the hygiene CI job has no node_modules for).
PM distributes no weights. The user's own Ollama fetches them from the publisher, so this is
disclosure, not enforcement — which is why `terms[].summary` is written to be read by a person.

apache-2.0.name: Apache License 2.0
apache-2.0.summary: A permissive open-source licence. Use, change and redistribute the model freely, including commercially; keep the notices and you are done. Nothing restricts what you may use it for.

mit.name: MIT License
mit.summary: A permissive open-source licence. Use, change and redistribute the model freely, including commercially, as long as the copyright notice travels with it. Nothing restricts what you may use it for.

gemma.name: Gemma Terms of Use
gemma.summary: Google's own terms, not an open-source licence. You may use and redistribute Gemma models commercially, but you must pass these terms on to anyone you share them with and follow Google's Prohibited Use Policy, which Google can change. Google may restrict any use it considers to be in breach.

llama3.1.name: Llama 3.1 Community License
llama3.1.summary: Meta's own licence, not an open-source one. Free to use and change, including commercially, but you must display "Built with Llama", pass the licence on with the model, and follow Meta's Acceptable Use Policy. A product with more than 700 million monthly active users needs a separate licence from Meta.

llama3.2.name: Llama 3.2 Community License
llama3.2.summary: Meta's own licence, not an open-source one. Free to use and change, including commercially, but you must display "Built with Llama", pass the licence on with the model, and follow Meta's Acceptable Use Policy. A product with more than 700 million monthly active users needs a separate licence from Meta.

qwen.name: Qwen License Agreement
qwen.summary: Alibaba's own licence, not an open-source one — and it governs this model even though the smaller Qwen 2.5 models are Apache-2.0. Free to use and change, including commercially, but you must keep its attribution notice and display "Built with Qwen" on anything you train from it. A product with more than 100 million monthly active users needs a separate licence from Alibaba.

unsloth/gemma-4-12b-it-GGUF.note: Gemma 4 is Apache-2.0, unlike Gemma 2 and 3. Google's own repo declares `apache-2.0` and is ungated, where every `google/gemma-2-*` and `google/gemma-3-*` is `gated: manual` under the Gemma Terms. The card's `license_link` still points at ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/gemma_4_license, which is a page titled "Apache License 2.0" — so the link is Gemma-branded but the licence is not.
